ablation.note: train_on=normal only changes the unsupervised models; rf always sees both classes

protocol.split: stratified on the binary label, new split per seed
protocol.threshold: max F1 on the validation split, applied unchanged to KDDTest+
protocol.fixed_fpr_thresholds: highest-recall threshold with at most 1% / 5% false alarms on the validation normal rows, applied unchanged to KDDTest+
protocol.oracle_test_max_f1: LEAK, reported only to measure it: max-F1 threshold chosen on KDDTest+ labels
protocol.quantile_thresholds: label-free: the 95th / 99th percentile of the scores of ALL validation flows (no labels used), so about 5% / 1% of validation flows alert; the false-alarm rate on normal traffic is whatever that gives
protocol.precision_prev: recall * p / (recall * p + fpr * (1 - p)) for attack base rate p = 1% and 10%; assumes the test recall and fpr carry over to that base rate
protocol.gaps: test minus validation; f1_gap also moves with the attack prevalence, fpr_gap does not
protocol.scaler: fit on the training split only
protocol.transform: log1p on ['duration', 'src_bytes', 'dst_bytes', 'hot', 'num_compromised', 'num_root', 'num_file_creations', 'count', 'srv_count'] before scaling (per-value, so no split leakage)
protocol.tuning: with --tune each model tries its grid (GRIDS in evaluate.py) and keeps the setting with the best PR-AUC on the validation split; the first grid entry is the untuned setting

test_groups.seen: attack type appears anywhere in KDDTrain+ (fixed across seeds)
